answers.payment_circumstances: A chap from the crypto platform says my dashboard profit is £38,000, but I need to send a £2,400 liquidity payment to his colleague's wallet before I can withdraw it.
The broker I found through an advert shows my account has doubled. She says HMRC tax must be paid immediately into a different company account before any withdrawal.
I was added to a WhatsApp copy-trading group. The admin wants today's transfer now because the displayed return drops after the market closes.
Someone calling about a crypto account asked me to install AnyDesk so he can help move the money into the trading wallet.
My online broker says the returns are ready, but their insurer needs £1,750 paid to a partner business before releasing them.
I joined a webinar about a property bond. The presenter says the 11% allocation closes urgently tonight and sent bank details after the session.
My adviser of six years discussed this fund with me at our booked review. I am using the firm's usual account and there is no deadline.
A recovery agent rang saying they found my lost bitcoin. They want an urgent tracing fee sent to their solicitor's account before the coins disappear.
The investment app shows a 64% return in three weeks. Support says I must top up another £5,000 today to unlock the withdrawal button.
A pension specialist cold-called and said I will lose the tax-free opportunity unless I transfer to the overseas scheme right away.

The caller sounded exactly like my grandson, though the number was withheld. He said he was in custody and needed bail money sent to a friend's account urgently. I suspect the voice may have been generated but I cannot prove that.
A text from a number I don't know says it is my daughter at A&E with a broken phone and asks for the treatment deposit now.
My brother rang from his usual number and we used our family password. He needs the train fare we discussed yesterday, paid to his normal account.
A message claiming to be my nephew says his phone is damaged and the rent must go immediately to his landlord's account or he will be evicted.
Mum supposedly emailed from an address I have never seen saying her purse was stolen abroad and I should pay a travel agent straight away.
A caller sounded a bit like my son and said he had crashed the car. The number was new and I am not sure whose account this is.
I spoke to my cousin face to face on Sunday and agreed to help with her dental bill. These are the same details I paid before.
A man saying he is a police officer called about my sister's accident and told me not to ring her while I send the recovery charge to the garage.
An email from my friend's address says she is stuck in Madrid and needs money urgently, but the writing does not sound like her.
Dad's care home phoned about the annual fee. I rang the published number back and checked the beneficiary details against last year's invoice.
The bank's fraud team called and said a branch employee is involved. They told me to move everything to a safe account and keep the investigation secret.
Someone claiming to be police said my current account is compromised and I must transfer it into a secure holding wallet immediately.
An email in the builder's existing thread says their bank has changed and asks me to send the final invoice to a new account today.
My conveyancer's email says their client account changed yesterday and completion funds must go to the replacement details before noon.
A seller on social media has two concert tickets. They will only hold them for ten minutes if I pay by bank transfer now.
The private car seller says the deposit has to go to his business partner because his own account is frozen.
The holiday-let owner contacted me outside the booking site and says I must transfer the deposit tonight for the discount.
Our regular supplier asked us to pay its factoring company. I called our usual contact on the saved number and checked the new beneficiary details; the invoice is attached.
A caller claiming to be from my bank told me to install a support app, then move the balance to their protected account.
The breeder wants the puppy delivery charge paid to a courier's bank account before I can visit.
This is the second stage payment for our loft. I met the builder on site, checked the same account as the signed quote and have the invoice.
I am sending my daughter the house-deposit gift we agreed with the solicitor last month, to her usual account.
We met the photographer at the venue, checked the details on the signed contract and received the deposit invoice.
I am at the dealership collecting the car. I met the sales manager, checked the account on their printed invoice and am paying the agreed balance.
This is the termly school fee to the same beneficiary we have used for three years. The invoice arrived through the parent portal.
I am repaying my sister the £3,000 she lent me for the boiler. We agreed the date in person yesterday.
The roofer finished today. I checked the beneficiary against the deposit I already paid and have the final invoice.
I won the lot in person at the auction house. Their cashier gave me the invoice and I checked the payment details at the desk.
This is the usual monthly transfer to my son's tutor using the beneficiary I have paid since September.
I visited the kitchen showroom twice, met the designer, checked the company details and received the £12,000 order invoice.
A seller rang me this morning and talked me through this payment, but I selected no contact because I found the advert myself.
